transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

What finally made me call the employee assistance program was the sleep. I lie awake replaying work stuff and arguments at home, then I wake up around three or four and can’t really get back to sleep. I start the day feeling like I never rested.
How long has this pattern of trouble sleeping and early waking been going on?
About a year and two months, I think. It started around when the arguments at home got a lot worse.
Over this past year, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah, most days. It’s like this heavy, gray mood follows me from the office to the car and then home. Even when nothing particular is going on, I just feel sort of hollow.
Over this past year, has your mood stayed at roughly the same level the whole time, or was there a point where it became noticeably worse or more intense, like a clear shift into a harder episode?
I’m not sure there was one clear point where it suddenly got worse. It’s felt pretty consistently heavy over the year, maybe some days are worse than others, but not like a distinct shift.

Aside from the mood and sleep issues, have you been feeling excessively worried or on edge about multiple areas of your life—like work, finances, or relationships—more days than not over this past year?
I’m not sure I’d call it worry exactly. I’ve mostly just felt low and tired, rather than constantly on edge about everything.

Besides the low mood and sleep trouble, have you noticed changes in your appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or any thoughts of death or wanting to hurt yourself over this past year?
I’m not making any plan to hurt myself, but… I do sometimes think that maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up one morning. It comes up more than I’d like to admit.
Over this past year, have you noticed trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, like at work, more days than not?

Yeah, pretty often. I used to get through sales forecasts and client decks quickly, but now I’ll read the same slide five times, second-guess every number, and still not be able to decide what I want to say.

Before things got worse with the arguments about 14 months ago, had you already been feeling this same kind of low, tired mood at a milder level for a longer stretch of time—maybe a year or more before that?
No, I don’t think so. It really started around a year and two months ago, when the arguments at home got a lot worse.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or took on many new projects or risks?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you ever had a similar period of low mood, low energy, and loss of interest at any earlier point in your life, before this past year?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of an earlier time that was like this.

How much are these mood, sleep, and concentration problems affecting your ability to function at work and in your daily life—for example, are you still able to keep up with your usual responsibilities, or has it become very hard to manage even basic tasks?

I’m still showing up to work, but I’m not keeping up the way I used to. My forecasts and client prep slip sometimes, and my team has had to cover for me. At home, I’m there, but… I’m less present with my wife and kids than I used to be.
You mentioned sometimes thinking everyone would be better off if you didn't wake up—can you tell me how often these thoughts occur and how intense or hard to shake they feel when they come?
It comes up more than I want to admit. I’m not making any plan to hurt myself, but sometimes I think maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up one morning.
